newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovakia extends Radio Free Europe licence.
newsitem.headline: Slovakia extends Radio Free Europe licence.

text.p: Slovakia on Tuesday extended for 18 months the broadcast licence for U.S.-sponsored Radio Free Europe (RFE) which has been accused by Slovak officials as having an anti-Slovak bias.
The decision by the Slovak Council for Radio and Television Broadcasting came six weeks before the expiration of RFE's licence.
At a public hearing earlier on Tuesday, members of the Broadcasting Council criticised RFE for giving airtime to mainly anti-government journalists and commentators.
"RFE often unjustifiably accuses Slovakia of being undemocratic," Council Chairman Peter Juras said.
RFE Slovak editor Miroslav Neovesky rejected the criticism saying RFE strived for maximum objectivity and integrity.
"The Slovak service of RFE does everything to provide its listeners with the broadest, most balanced and objective information," Neovesky told the council.
The Broadcasting Council is nominated by parliament in which the ruling coalition led by Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar has a majority.
Last year the Council extended the licence of Prague-based RFE for only one year after criticising the radio service for biased reporting.

In March 1994, the Slovak Ministry of Communications shut down three transmitters broadcasting RFE programmes after government complaints that the station was biased against Meciar and his administration.

Broadcasting was resumed after a few days when a new Slovak government was installed following a parliamentary vote of no-confidence in Meciar. He then returned to power after extraordinary elections that autumn.
